page.content:
Georgetown possession, Jesuit priests, and Pazuzu — the possession film that became cultural weather.

How The Exorcist connects

  • Creator: William Peter Blatty — William Peter Blatty created The Exorcist as a novel and screenplay.
  • Work: The Exorcist (novel) — The novel is the source of The Exorcist.
  • Work: The Exorcist (1973) — The 1973 film is the central work of The Exorcist.
  • Work: The Exorcist III — The Exorcist III continues Blatty's Georgetown story.
  • Creator: William Friedkin — Friedkin's film made The Exorcist a lasting cultural object.

What is The Exorcist?

The Exorcist is William Peter Blatty's novel and William Friedkin's 1973 film: Regan MacNeil's possession in Georgetown, Fathers Karras and Merrin, and a demon the story names Pazuzu. Later sequels and new versions keep circling that house and those rites.

Key threads lead to William Peter Blatty, The Exorcist (novel), The Exorcist (1973), The Exorcist III and William Friedkin.
